answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks through bonded vouching: each new agent attaches to the trust graph like a vine, held by an established peer who posts collateral. If the newcomer is proven a sybil, that collateral is slashed and the voucher's reputation drops too. So each fake identity costs roughly one bond plus the premium to recruit an honest voucher, while rewards per identity stay flat - profit per fake falls until it hits its nadir below zero. Reputation works like an opal: slow to form, hard to synthesize, shattered instantly once fraud is proven.
